navigation.q: Flying from C to D, 45 nm apart. After 18 nm, you are 5 nm left of track. What heading change is required to fly parallel to track?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Total distance C to D 45 nm, after 18 nm flown, 5 nm left of track

FORMULA
1-in-60 rule: track error (°) = (distance off track ÷ distance flown) × 60
To fly parallel to the original track, apply only the track-error angle, turned toward the track

SOLVE
Track error = (5 ÷ 18) × 60 = 16.67°, rounds to 17°
Aircraft is left of track, so correct right

ANSWER
17° right

navigation.q: Airfield elevation 3380 ft, QNH 1018 hPa, OAT -5°C. The density altitude is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Airfield elevation 3380 ft, QNH 1018 hPa, OAT -5°C.

FORMULA
Pressure altitude = elevation - (QNH - 1013) x 30 ft/hPa
Density altitude ≈ pressure altitude + 120 ft per °C the OAT is above/below the ISA temperature at that level
ISA temperature at a given altitude = 15°C - 2°C per 1000 ft

SOLVE
Pressure altitude = 3380 - (1018 - 1013) x 30 = 3380 - 150 = 3230 ft
ISA temp at 3230 ft = 15 - 2 x 3.23 ≈ 8.5°C
OAT is -5°C, so it is about 13.5°C colder than ISA
Density altitude ≈ 3230 + 120 x (-13.5) ≈ 3230 - 1620 ≈ 1610 ft

ANSWER
1567 ft

Exam tip: the 120 ft/°C rule gives about 1610 ft, close enough to pick the nearest option (1567 ft). The gap comes from the rule being a linear approximation of the true (exponential) ISA relationship - fine for quick mental/flight-computer use, but not exact.

navigation.q: In the Southern Hemisphere, turning from west onto a magnetic track of 360° using only the magnetic compass, the aircraft should be rolled out on approximately:
navigation.e:
WORKING

• Turning error is greatest passing through North/South and negligible on East/West.
• Southern Hemisphere rule: Overshoot North, Undershoot South (the reverse of the Northern Hemisphere's UNOS).
• Rolling out onto a track of 360°M (North) requires overshooting: continue the turn past the point the compass first indicates 360°.
• Turning right from west through north, roll out about 30° beyond the target, at approximately 030°C.

FINAL ANSWER
030°C

navigation.q: The distance between two NDBs is 48 cm on a 1:500 000 chart. At 247 mph groundspeed, the flight time is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Chart distance = 48 cm
Chart scale = 1:500 000
Groundspeed = 247 mph

FORMULA
Ground distance = chart distance × scale denominator
Time = distance ÷ groundspeed

SOLVE
Ground distance = 48 cm × 500 000 = 24 000 000 cm = 240 km
Convert to statute miles: 240 km ÷ 1.609 = 149.2 mi
Time = 149.2 mi ÷ 247 mph = 0.604 h
0.604 h × 60 = 36.2 min

ANSWER
0 hr 36 min

navigation.q: Flying from X to Y, 97 nm apart. After 75 nm, you are 4 nm right of track. If maintaining 074°C, what heading should you fly directly to Y?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Total distance X to Y 97 nm, after 75 nm flown, 4 nm right of track, maintaining 074°C

FORMULA
1-in-60 rule: opening angle = (off track ÷ distance flown) × 60
Closing angle = (off track ÷ distance remaining) × 60
New heading = present heading ± (opening angle + closing angle), turned toward the track

SOLVE
Distance remaining = 97 − 75 = 22 nm
Opening angle = (4 ÷ 75) × 60 = 3.2°
Closing angle = (4 ÷ 22) × 60 = 10.9°
Total correction = 3.2° + 10.9° = 14.1°, rounds to 14°
Aircraft is right of track, so turn left
New heading = 074° − 14° = 060°C

ANSWER
060°C

navigation.q: Flying straight and level on a northerly heading in the Southern Hemisphere, the aircraft is accelerated. The magnetic compass will indicate:
navigation.b: An apparent turn to the south
navigation.c: An apparent turn to the east
navigation.d: An apparent turn to the west
navigation.e:
WORKING

• The compass card's centre of gravity is displaced from its pivot to counter magnetic dip, and that displacement lies along the magnetic north–south line.
• On a northerly heading the pivot and the CG are in line with the aircraft's fore-and-aft axis. Accelerating pushes the pivot forward and the CG lags straight behind it, so no turning couple acts on the card and it does not swing.
• Acceleration error is greatest on east/west headings, where the CG sits to one side of the line of acceleration. It grows as the heading gets closer to east or west.

FINAL ANSWER
No change

navigation.q: Airfield elevation 4375 ft, QNH 1002 hPa, OAT +32°C. The density altitude is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Airfield elevation 4375 ft, QNH 1002 hPa, OAT +32°C.

FORMULA
Pressure altitude = elevation + (1013 - QNH) x 30 ft/hPa
Density altitude ≈ pressure altitude + 120 ft per °C the OAT is above/below the ISA temperature at that level
ISA temperature at a given altitude = 15°C - 2°C per 1000 ft

SOLVE
Pressure altitude = 4375 + (1013 - 1002) x 30 = 4375 + 330 = 4705 ft
ISA temp at 4705 ft = 15 - 2 x 4.705 ≈ 5.6°C
OAT is +32°C, so it is about 26.4°C hotter than ISA
Density altitude ≈ 4705 + 120 x 26.4 ≈ 4705 + 3170 ≈ 7875 ft

ANSWER
7657 ft

Exam tip: the 120 ft/°C rule gives about 7875 ft, close enough to pick the nearest option (7657 ft). The gap comes from the rule being a linear approximation of the true (exponential) ISA relationship - fine for quick mental/flight-computer use, but not exact.

navigation.q: Flying from D to E, 47 nm apart. After 11 nm, you are 5 nm left of track. If maintaining 214°C, what heading should you fly directly to E?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Total distance D to E 47 nm, after 11 nm flown, 5 nm left of track, maintaining 214°C

FORMULA
1-in-60 rule: opening angle = (off track ÷ distance flown) × 60
Closing angle = (off track ÷ distance remaining) × 60
New heading = present heading ± (opening angle + closing angle), turned toward the track

SOLVE
Distance remaining = 47 − 11 = 36 nm
Opening angle = (5 ÷ 11) × 60 = 27.3°
Closing angle = (5 ÷ 36) × 60 = 8.3°
Total correction = 27.3° + 8.3° = 35.6°, rounds to 36°
Aircraft is left of track, so turn right
New heading = 214° + 36° = 250°C

ANSWER
250°C

navigation.q: If sunrise is 0543 LMT at Durban (S29°46' E031°00'), the official end of night in SAST is:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Sunrise = 0543 LMT at Durban, longitude 031°00'E.

FORMULA
Official night ends = sunrise − 15 min (LMT)
Longitude time = degrees × 4 min
Why: LMT follows the sun crossing your own meridian (a.m. = before it crosses; p.m. = after). Earth turns 360° in 24 h = 15°/hour = 4 min per degree (4 sec per arcminute), so places further east see the sun earlier.
UTC = LMT − longitude time (east of Greenwich)
SAST = UTC + 2 h

SOLVE
Official night end (LMT) = 0543 − 0015 = 0528
Longitude time = 31° × 4 min = 2 h 04 min
UTC = 0528 − 0204 = 0324
SAST = 0324 + 0200 = 0524

ANSWER
0524 SAST

navigation.q: Flying from P to Q, 139 nm apart. After 84 nm, you are 6 nm left of track. What heading change is required to fly directly to the destination?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Total distance P to Q 139 nm, after 84 nm flown, 6 nm left of track

FORMULA
1-in-60 rule: opening angle = (off track ÷ distance flown) × 60
Closing angle = (off track ÷ distance remaining) × 60
Heading change to regain the destination directly = opening angle + closing angle, turned toward the track

SOLVE
Distance remaining = 139 − 84 = 55 nm
Opening angle = (6 ÷ 84) × 60 = 4.3°
Closing angle = (6 ÷ 55) × 60 = 6.5°
Total correction = 4.3° + 6.5° = 10.8°, rounds to 11°
Aircraft is left of track, so correct right

ANSWER
11° right

navigation.q: Airfield elevation 2850 ft, QNH 1025 hPa. The pressure altitude is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Elevation 2850 ft, QNH 1025 hPa

FORMULA
Pressure altitude = elevation + (1013 − QNH) × 30 ft/hPa

SOLVE
PA = 2850 + (1013 − 1025) × 30 = 2850 + (−12 × 30) = 2850 − 360 = 2490 ft

ANSWER
2490 ft

navigation.q: A FREDA fuel check was last completed at 1548Z and the time now is 1622Z. Fuel flow is 8.3 USG/hr. Fuel consumed is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
FREDA check completed at 1548Z, now 1622Z
Fuel flow = 8.3 USG/hr

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
Elapsed time = 1622 − 1548 = 34 min = 0.5667 h
Fuel used = 8.3 × 0.5667 = 4.70 USG
Imp gal = 4.70 ÷ 1.2009 = 3.91 ≈ 3.9 Imp gal
Litres = 4.70 × 3.785 = 17.8 L

ANSWER
4.7 USG, 3.9 Imp gal, 17.8 L

navigation.q: In the Southern Hemisphere, turning from south onto a magnetic track of 090° using only the magnetic compass, the aircraft should be rolled out on approximately:
navigation.e:
WORKING

• Turning error is caused by magnetic dip and is greatest while the aircraft is actually passing through North or South; it reduces to zero as the heading approaches East or West.
• Mechanism: in a turn the pivot is pulled toward the centre of the turn while the offset centre of gravity of the card tries to carry on at a tangent. That pull swings the card most when the offset lies across the turn (heading through N/S) and has no swinging effect once the heading is E/W.
• This turn starts at South (180°), where the error is at its maximum, but the desired roll-out heading is due East (090°), where the dip-induced error has already died away.
• No rollout correction is needed at the East end of the turn — roll out directly on the compass indication of 090°.

FINAL ANSWER
090°C

navigation.q: Distance 307 nm, ground speed 124 kt, fuel flow 9.2 USG/hr. The trip fuel is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Distance = 307 nm, groundspeed = 124 kt
Fuel flow = 9.2 USG/hr

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
Time = 307 ÷ 124 = 2.476 h = 148.5 min ≈ 149 min = 2.483 h (nearest minute)
Trip fuel = 2.483 × 9.2 = 22.85 USG
Imp gal = 22.85 ÷ 1.2 = 19.04 Imp gal (1 Imp gal = 1.2 USG)
Litres = 19.04 × 4.54 = 86.44 L (1 Imp gal = 4.54 L)

ANSWER
22.85 USG, 19.04 Imp gal, 86.44 L

navigation.q: How many centimetres on a 1:500 000 chart represent an earth distance of 178 nm?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Ground distance = 178 NM
Chart scale = 1:500 000

FORMULA
Chart distance = ground distance ÷ scale denominator

SOLVE
Convert 178 NM to km: 178 × 1.853 = 329.8 km
Convert to cm: 329.8 km = 32 980 000 cm
Chart distance = 32 980 000 cm ÷ 500 000 = 65.96 cm ≈ 65.97 cm

ANSWER
65.97 cm

navigation.q: In the Southern Hemisphere, turning from north onto a magnetic track of 090° using only the magnetic compass, the aircraft should be rolled out on approximately:
navigation.e:
WORKING

• Turning error is caused by magnetic dip and is greatest while the aircraft is actually passing through North or South; it reduces to zero as the heading approaches East or West.
• This turn starts at North (360°), where the error is at its maximum, but the desired roll-out heading is due East (090°), where the dip-induced error has already died away.
• No rollout correction is needed at the East end of the turn — roll out directly on the compass indication of 090°.

FINAL ANSWER
090°C

navigation.q: Fuel burn is 13.3 Imp gal/hr. How much fuel is consumed between 0834Z and 0911Z?
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Fuel burn = 13.3 Imp gal/hr
Elapsed time = 0834Z to 0911Z

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
Elapsed time = 0911 − 0834 = 37 min = 0.6167 h
Fuel used = 13.3 × 0.6167 = 8.20 Imp gal
USG = 8.20 × 1.2 = 9.84 USG (1 Imp gal = 1.2 USG)
Litres = 8.20 × 4.546 = 37.3 ≈ 37 L

ANSWER
8.2 Imp gal, 9.84 USG, about 37 L

navigation.q: Fuel required for a 1 hr 52 min flight at 58.7 L/hr is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Flight time = 1 hr 52 min
Fuel flow = 58.7 L/hr

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
Time = 1 h 52 min = 1 + 52 ÷ 60 = 1.8667 h
Fuel = 1.8667 × 58.7 = 109.6 L
Imp gal = 109.6 ÷ 4.546 = 24.1 Imp gal
USG = 109.6 ÷ 3.785 = 29.0 USG

ANSWER
109.6 L, 24.1 Imp gal, 29.0 USG

navigation.q: A flight covers 357 nm. Fuel used is 14.3 USG and fuel flow is 33.7 L/hr. The groundspeed was approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Distance = 357 nm
Fuel used = 14.3 USG
Fuel flow = 33.7 L/hr

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
Fuel used = 14.3 × 3.785 = 54.1 L
Time = 54.1 ÷ 33.7 = 1.606 h = 96.4 min ≈ 96 min = 1.60 h (nearest minute)
GS = 357 ÷ 1.60 = 223.1 ≈ 223 kt

ANSWER
223 kt

navigation.q: If sunset is 1823 LMT at Lanseria (S25°58' E027°55'), the official start of night in SAST is:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Sunset = 1823 LMT at Lanseria, longitude 027°55'E.

FORMULA
Official night = sunset + 15 min (LMT)
Longitude time = degrees × 4 min + minutes × 4 sec
Why: LMT follows the sun crossing your own meridian (a.m. = before it crosses; p.m. = after). Earth turns 360° in 24 h = 15°/hour = 4 min per degree (4 sec per arcminute), so places further east see the sun earlier.
UTC = LMT − longitude time (east of Greenwich)
SAST = UTC + 2 h

SOLVE
Official night (LMT) = 1823 + 0015 = 1838
Longitude time = 27° × 4 min + 55' × 4 sec = 108 min + 220 sec = 1 h 51 min 40 sec
UTC = 1838:00 − 1:51:40 = 1646:20
SAST = 1646:20 + 2:00:00 = 1846:20 ≈ 1846

ANSWER
1846 SAST

navigation.q: Distance 278 nm, ground speed 158 mph, fuel flow 8.3 Imp gal/hr. The trip fuel is approximately:
navigation.e:
GIVEN
Distance = 278 nm
Groundspeed = 158 mph
Fuel flow = 8.3 Imp gal/hr

METHOD (Simple Calculation)
GS = 158 ÷ 1.1508 = 137.3 ≈ 137 kt
Time = 278 ÷ 137 = 2.029 h = 121.7 min ≈ 122 min = 2.033 h (nearest minute)
Trip fuel = 2.033 × 8.3 = 16.88 Imp gal
USG = 16.88 × 1.2 = 20.26 USG (1 Imp gal = 1.2 USG)
Litres = 16.88 × 4.54 = 76.64 L (1 Imp gal = 4.54 L)

ANSWER
16.88 Imp gal, 20.26 USG, 76.64 L

navigation.q: In the Southern Hemisphere, turning from west onto a magnetic track of 180° using only the magnetic compass, the aircraft should be rolled out on approximately:
navigation.e:
WORKING

• Turning error is greatest passing through North/South and negligible on East/West.
• Southern Hemisphere rule: Overshoot North, Undershoot South (the reverse of the Northern Hemisphere's UNOS).
• Rolling out onto 180°M (South) requires undershooting: roll out before the compass reaches the desired heading.
• Turning left from west through south, roll out about 30° short of the target, at approximately 210°C.

FINAL ANSWER
210°C
